analysis.title: Textron Inc. (TXT): Mixed fundamentals keep us Neutral
key_insights: GS keeps TXT at Neutral with a 12m price target of $94 ($93 prior) against a $85.70 price, 9.7% upside. The target is based on 9.0X 2027E EV/EBITDA, unchanged.
3Q26 adjusted EPS was $1.76 against FactSet consensus of $1.43 and a GS estimate of $1.51. Total revenue was about 1% below FactSet consensus and manufacturing segment EBIT was 2% above.
Total revenue was $3,740mn against a GS estimate of $3,751mn, up 4.1% y/y. Total operating margin was 9.5% against 9.9% a year ago, down 40bps y/y.

Aviation revenue rose 13.7% y/y on higher aircraft and aftermarket parts and services revenue. Aviation EBIT margin fell 140bps y/y to 10.7% on manufacturing inefficiencies and mix. GS says aviation demand is solid but delivery growth is constrained and margins have been sluggish this year as TXT works through supply chain and other disruptions.
Aviation backlog was flat sequentially and up 4% y/y at $8.0bn. Implied book-to-bill was 0.98X in the quarter and 1.05X over the last twelve months.

Bell revenue fell 9.1% y/y on lower military revenue. EBIT margin fell 90bps y/y to 8.1%. GS expects high long-term growth from the MV75 program, but medium-term EBIT is limited by mix and the LRIP (low-rate initial production) structure.
Bell backlog was up 1% sequentially at $7.6bn, with quarterly book-to-bill of 1.07X and TTM book-to-bill of 0.88X.

Systems revenue rose 17.3% y/y on new products in high-priority areas. EBIT margin fell 110bps y/y to 15.8%. Backlog rose 5% sequentially to $3.5bn, with book-to-bill of 1.42X in the quarter and 1.22X TTM.
Industrial revenue rose 0.5% y/y and EBIT margin rose 90bps y/y to 5.0%.
Adjusted free cash flow was $418mn against $281mn a year ago, and TXT repurchased $239mn of shares in the quarter.

TXT raised 2026 guidance: adjusted EPS to $6.55-6.65 from $6.40-6.60 (consensus $6.42), and manufacturing cash flow to $800-900mn from $700-800mn. Capex guidance was cut to about $550mn from about $650mn.
GS raised EPS estimates to $6.63 for 2026, $7.22 for 2027 and $8.37 for 2028, from $6.47, $7.12 and $8.19, on changes to segment revenue and margins. 2029E and 2030E are $9.47 and $10.57.
GS says valuation is not demanding but the fundamental picture across segments is mixed. The stock is at 12.9X 2026E P/E and 8.1X 2026E EV/EBITDA.
Key risks named are business jet demand, new program execution and DoD spending.

market_movers.rationale: GS raised the target from $93 and kept Neutral after 3Q26. Aviation demand is solid but margins are sluggish, Bell's medium-term EBIT is limited by mix and LRIP, and Systems is growing fast.

sector_views.rationale: For TXT, GS sees mixed fundamentals across segments. Aviation margins are pressured, Bell growth is back-end loaded, and Systems is growing from new products.

earnings_insights: TXT 3Q26 adjusted diluted EPS reported at $1.76 (continuing ops) versus FactSet consensus of $1.43 and GS estimate of $1.51, and $1.55 a year earlier (3Q25), up 13.6% y/y.
TXT 3Q26 total revenue reported at $3,740mn versus GS estimate of $3,751mn, up 4.1% y/y, and about 1% below FactSet consensus.
TXT 3Q26 manufacturing segment operating profit reported at $337mn versus GS estimate of $350mn, up 3.2% y/y. GS says it was 2% above consensus.
Revenue and margins were above consensus at Aviation and Systems, and below at Bell and Industrial.
The effective tax rate was 24.6% versus 19.3% in the GS estimate and 30.1% a year ago.

2026 guidance (company): adjusted EPS $6.55-6.65, up from $6.40-6.60 in January, against consensus of $6.42. Manufacturing cash flow $800-900mn versus $700-800mn prior. Total revenue about $15.5bn, capex about $550mn versus about $650mn prior.
risk_factors: Aviation supply chain disruptions and manufacturing inefficiencies
Bell medium-term margin limits from mix and the LRIP structure
